title: The past that never was
description: Say what would have happened, or what you hoped for.

explanation.summary: The past subjunctive is used for things that did not happen, or that may still not have happened. In English it survives only in a few formulas, so it is worth learning as a set of phrases.

sections.heading: How it is formed
sections.body: Take the yo form of the preterite and use the -ra endings: habló becomes hablara, comió becomes comiera, vivió becomes viviera. There is a second form with -se, and it means the same thing in almost every case: hablase, comiese. Use -ra, because it is the one you hear.

examples.en: If I had time, I would travel.

examples.es: Como si fuera experto, no hablaría.
examples.en: As if I were an expert, I would not speak.

sections.heading: Where it appears
sections.body: After si with an unreal condition: si tuviera, si pudiera. After como si, as if. After ojalá, a wish. After the past tenses of wishing or doubting: esperaba que viniera. And in polite requests about the past: quisiera un café.

examples.en: I would like a coffee, please.
I was hoping you would arrive on time.
If I could, I would help you.

exercises.note: The past subjunctive is the -ra form: hablara, comiera, viviera.
